questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q01 Draft problem: A peer says the ending is unclear because the reader cannot tell why the character leaves. What is the best next step?\

answer.text: A. Change every character name.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Names do not address motivation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Add or revise a moment that shows the character's reason for leaving.

feedback.text: Correct. This responds directly to the feedback. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Ignore the feedback because all endings are confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Feedback should be considered. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Add random punctuation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Punctuation will not clarify motivation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q02 Workshop context: Which feedback is most useful?\

answer.text: A. I do not like stories like this.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal preference. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. It is good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Change everything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too broad. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The repeated hallway image builds tension; consider clarifying what the character fears at the end.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a strength and a focused suggestion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q03 Format context: A script has dialogue but no character labels. What should be revised?\

answer.text: A. Add clear speaker labels and useful stage directions.

feedback.text: Correct. This supports script readability. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Remove all dialogue.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Dialogue is central to script form. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Add random stanza breaks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Stanza breaks do not solve script speaker clarity.

answer.text: D. Ignore formatting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Format matters. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q04 Which answer best explains author craft reasoning?\

answer.text: A. I like my poem.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is opinion. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The poem has words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I placed the final image on its own line so the reader pauses before the speaker's decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a craft choice and reader effect.

answer.text: D. I wrote it quickly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Speed is not craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q05 Which piece is most publication-ready?\

answer.text: A. A rough draft with no title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It lacks readiness checks. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A script with no speaker labels.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This has a format issue. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A story with random spacing and no review.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random spacing and no review weaken readiness.

answer.text: D. A revised poem with purposeful line breaks, checked conventions, clear title, and appropriate content.

feedback.text: Correct. This includes revision, format, conventions, and audience readiness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q06 Feedback says a paragraph is confusing because two speakers are in one paragraph. Which revision best fits?\

answer.text: A. Add more unrelated setting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue is speaker clarity. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Start a new paragraph when the speaker changes and check dialogue tags.

feedback.text: Correct. This improves clarity and format. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Change the title only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The title does not solve dialogue confusion.

answer.text: D. Delete all dialogue.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A targeted revision is better. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q07 Which answer should be eliminated first?\

answer.text: A. Accept every suggestion automatically.

feedback.text: Correct. Automatic acceptance can damage purpose and voice.

answer.text: B. Consider feedback and protect the writer's purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is strong. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Explain reader effect.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reader effect is important. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Check format before publication.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Format checks are important. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q08 A portfolio note should include what?\

answer.text: A. Only "I like it."

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Private personal information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is inappropriate. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Selection reason, revision evidence, and final readiness explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. This supports portfolio readiness. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A list of random colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That does not explain writing growth. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q09 Which is the best author presentation opening?\

answer.text: A. My story has stuff in it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I will tell the whole plot first.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This over-summarizes. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I do not know why I wrote it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This lacks purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. "Open Door" is a short story meant to show a character deciding whether to trust someone again.

feedback.text: Correct. This names title, form, and purpose. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q10 Which revision most directly improves reader effect?\

answer.text: A. Replacing "I was sad" with an image of the last bus passing without stopping.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows emotion through image. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Changing the font randomly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not improve the writing itself.

answer.text: C. Deleting the title for no reason.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That may weaken reader preparation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Ignoring feedback about clarity.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That does not improve reader effect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q11 What is active listening in workshop?\

answer.text: A. Interrupting before the writer finishes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That blocks listening. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Restating the writer's purpose before giving feedback.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows understanding before response. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Giving only personal preference.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Feedback should be craft-focused. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Ignoring the writer's goal.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The goal matters. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q12 Which is a strong publication decision?\

answer.text: A. Post another student's work without permission.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That violates authorship. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Publish a rough draft without review.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Readiness checks are needed. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Mock peer writing in a comment.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication must be respectful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Use a school-appropriate excerpt and remove private identifying details.

feedback.text: Correct. This supports safe online publication. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q13 Which statement best separates revision and polishing?\

answer.text: A. Polishing fixes purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Purpose is a revision issue. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Revision means random changes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision is purposeful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Revision improves meaning or structure; polishing checks final details.

feedback.text: Correct. This separates major improvement from final cleanup.

answer.text: D. Polishing should happen before reading the draft.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Polishing comes after review. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q14 A poem uses random line breaks that make the central image hard to read. What should the writer do?\

answer.text: A. Revise line breaks so the image and pauses support the intended effect.

feedback.text: Correct. This improves format-specific quality. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Keep the random breaks because all poems must be confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Format should support meaning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Delete every image.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue is line breaks. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Ignore the reader.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reader understanding matters. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q15 Which response best explains a revision decision?\

answer.text: A. I changed it because I had to.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain improvement. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I shortened the ending because feedback showed the first version explained too much.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects feedback, change, and improvement. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I changed random words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random change is not revision reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I did not revise anything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q16 Which feedback is least helpful?\

answer.text: A. The opening image creates suspense.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This names a strength. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. What does the character want in the final scene?

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a useful question. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Consider adding one sound before the reveal.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a focused suggestion. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Make it better.

feedback.text: Correct. This is too vague to guide revision.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q17 Which checklist best fits Unit 5?\

answer.text: A. Type, post, ignore feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This skips the workflow. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Decorate randomly and submit.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random decoration is not readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Understand purpose, consider feedback, revise, check format and conventions, prepare readers, explain author reasoning.

feedback.text: Correct. This synthesizes the unit. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Summarize the plot only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Unit 5 includes more than summary. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q18 A writer's presentation retells every event but gives no craft reasoning. What is the best correction?\

answer.text: A. Focus on purpose, two craft choices, and one revision decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches author presentation expectations. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Add more plot summary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Summary is already the issue. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Remove the creative work entirely.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The work should remain central. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Avoid mentioning craft.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft reasoning is required. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q19 Which answer best handles online collaborative feedback?\

answer.text: A. Let reviewers erase the writer's purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Purpose should be protected. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Consider suggestions, accept what improves the piece, and reject what conflicts with purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. This is thoughtful collaboration. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Reject every comment automatically.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Some feedback may help. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Publish without review.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Review supports readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q20 Which convention issue should be fixed before publication?\

answer.text: A. A purposeful line break in a poem.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Purposeful line breaks may be effective. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A strong title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A strong title should remain. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A clear author note.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This supports publication. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Dialogue punctuation that makes speakers hard to follow.

feedback.text: Correct. This affects clarity. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q21 Which selection rationale is strongest?\

answer.text: A. I selected this story because revision from feedback clarified the character's decision and made the ending stronger.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects selection to growth. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I selected this because it was first in my folder.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is not a quality reason. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I selected this because I did not read the others.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is not purposeful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I selected this because it has no title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Missing title is not a strength. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q22 Which answer best identifies reader effect?\

answer.text: A. The writer changed something.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The shorter sentence slows the reader at the final decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. The piece exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not identify effect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The author used a computer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is irrelevant. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q23 Which is the strongest response to vague feedback?\

answer.text: A. Accept it without question.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Vague feedback needs clarification. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Delete the draft.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is extreme. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Ask for the specific place where the reader became confused.

feedback.text: Correct. This turns vague feedback into useful information.

answer.text: D. Ignore all future feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Feedback can help. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q24 Which author note is best for publication?\

answer.text: A. This piece is about everything and nothing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Do not read this.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not prepare readers. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I will explain every word.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overexplains. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. This poem uses the bus stop image to show waiting; I revised the final line so the speaker's choice is clearer.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives context and revision insight. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q25 Which response shows Unit 5 mastery?\

answer.text: A. I can type a rough draft and stop.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This skips the unit skills. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I can ignore readers and feedback.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reader effect and feedback matter. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I can use feedback to revise, check format and conventions, prepare work for publication, and explain craft choices to an audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This summarizes the unit's major skills.

answer.text: D. I can choose answers randomly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Mastery requires purposeful reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q26

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q26 Draft Excerpt: I walked into the room. It was weird. Something felt different. Feedback: I cannot picture the room. Which revision goal is best?\

answer.text: A. Change every sentence because the draft is bad.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision should be targeted, not random. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Add one specific detail that helps readers picture the room.

feedback.text: Correct. The feedback says the room is hard to picture, so a targeted setting detail directly addresses the issue.

answer.text: C. Delete the whole draft and start over.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The feedback names a specific issue, so a targeted revision is better.

answer.text: D. Add a new character with no connection to the room.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That does not solve the setting problem.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q27

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q27 Draft Excerpt: The poem is about missing my old neighborhood. Feedback: Add one concrete image from the neighborhood. Which revision best uses the feedback?\

answer.text: A. Add the image of the corner store sign flickering after rain.

feedback.text: Correct. This adds a concrete neighborhood image, which is exactly what the feedback requests.

answer.text: B. Add a sentence saying the poem is emotional.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That tells feeling but does not add a concrete image.

answer.text: C. Remove all details about the neighborhood.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That works against the feedback. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Change the poem into a research report.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The feedback asks for an image, not a new genre.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q28

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q28 Feedback: Make it better. How should this feedback be classified?\

answer.text: A. Specific and actionable.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It does not identify what needs improvement.

answer.text: B. A clear revision goal.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It is too general to be a goal.

answer.text: C. A convention correction.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It does not mention grammar, punctuation, or spelling.

answer.text: D. Vague and not actionable.

feedback.text: Correct. "Make it better" does not tell the writer what to revise or why.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q29

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q29 Draft Sentence: Mara handed Lena the box after she dropped it, and it made her upset. Which revision is clearest?\

answer.text: A. She handed it over after it happened and it was upsetting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This keeps the pronoun confusion. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. After Maya opened the box, she handed the old photograph to Lena.

feedback.text: Correct. This revision names the people and object clearly so the reader knows who did what.

answer.text: C. The box was there and it was a thing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. They did it and then it happened.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is even less clear. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q30

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q30 Draft: The rain stopped. I found the letter. The house was quiet. Which revision improves cohesion?\

answer.text: A. The rain stopped. I found the letter. The house was quiet.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This repeats the choppy original. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Letter quiet rain house found.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This removes sentence clarity. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. When the rain stopped, I found the letter on the quiet porch.

feedback.text: Correct. This combines the ideas smoothly and shows the relationship between events.

answer.text: D. I found quiet because rain letter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not coherent. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q31

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q31 Workshop context: A writer says, "I want this scene to feel tense but still clear." Which response best shows active listening?\

answer.text: A. You want the scene to create tension while the reader can still follow what is happening.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the writer's purpose clearly before giving feedback.

answer.text: B. I like funny scenes better.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This focuses on personal preference instead of the writer's purpose.

answer.text: C. You should change the whole scene.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This gives a broad command before showing that the purpose was understood.

answer.text: D. The scene is probably finished already.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This avoids listening for the writer's revision goal.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q32

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q32 Workshop context: A peer draft uses the line, "The porch light held its breath." Which feedback best names a craft strength?\

answer.text: A. I like porch lights.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is personal preference and does not explain the craft strength.

answer.text: B. You should write about a different house.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This changes the topic without explaining what is working.

answer.text: C. This is good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general to help the writer revise.

answer.text: D. The personification of the porch light creates a quiet, tense mood.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the craft move and explains its effect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q33

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q33 Draft Excerpt: I waited outside the rehearsal room. The music stopped. I raised my hand to knock, then lowered it. The writer wants a poem that emphasizes hesitation. Which format choice best fits?\

answer.text: A. Put the entire draft in one long line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. One long line may reduce the pause that shows hesitation.

answer.text: B. Use line breaks around "raised my hand" and "lowered it" so the reader pauses with the speaker.

feedback.text: Correct. The format choice supports pacing and meaning.

answer.text: C. Add random spaces between every word.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random spacing distracts the reader and does not clearly support meaning.

answer.text: D. Remove all punctuation and format choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Removing all control can make the piece harder to read.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q34

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q34 Draft Excerpt: "Come in" Mara said but she did not open the door. Which prose-story revision best improves publication quality?\

answer.text: A. "Come in," Mara said, but she did not open the door.

feedback.text: Correct. The punctuation and sentence control make the dialogue clear.

answer.text: B. come in mara said but she did not open the door

feedback.text: Incorrect. This removes punctuation and capitalization, which weakens readability.

answer.text: C. COME IN MARA SAID BUT SHE DID NOT OPEN THE DOORfor this item

feedback.text: Incorrect. All capitals do not create clear prose formatting.

answer.text: D. Come in. Mara. Door. Said.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This fragments the sentence and makes meaning less clear.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q35

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q35 Publication context: A student finishes typing a rough draft and wants to place it in the class online publication space immediately. What should happen first?\

answer.text: A. Post it immediately because typing means it is finished.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A typed draft still needs revision, format, and readiness checks.

answer.text: B. Delete the draft and start over.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The draft may be useful; it needs a publication workflow.

answer.text: C. Review purpose, feedback, format, audience appropriateness, and final conventions before publication.

feedback.text: Correct. Publication-ready work requires more than simply posting a draft.

answer.text: D. Change the title only and ignore the rest.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title is important, but it is not the only publication check.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q36

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q36 Collaborative publication context: Which role checks whether line breaks, paragraph breaks, title, and spacing fit the creative form?\

answer.text: A. Weather reporter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a publication role. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Unrelated reader.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The role needs a specific publication responsibility.

answer.text: C. Person who changes the writer's purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Collaboration should not erase the writer's purpose.

answer.text: D. Format checker.

feedback.text: Correct. The format checker reviews whether the piece's visual and structural choices support the form.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q37

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q37 Author presentation context: Which opening is strongest?\

answer.text: A. "After the Rain" is a short prose piece meant to show a character who is safe but still unsure how to move forward.

feedback.text: Correct. This names title, form, and purpose. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. My story has a driveway, rain, and an umbrella, and then things happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This mostly summarizes events without purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I do not know what my piece is about.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The author needs to frame the work clearly.

answer.text: D. The audience should figure out everything with no help.

feedback.text: Incorrect. An author presentation should provide a useful entry point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q38

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q38 Which sentence best explains craft reasoning?\

answer.text: A. I used an umbrella because umbrellas exist.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain craft purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I repeated the umbrella image so the reader could see the character holding onto protection even after the rain stopped.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the craft choice and explains reader effect.

answer.text: C. The story has words and sentences.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I made choices because writing needs choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain a specific reader effect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q39

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q39 Portfolio context: A writer chooses a story only because it is the shortest draft. What is the best correction?\

answer.text: A. Choose it automatically because short always means portfolio-ready.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length does not prove readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Choose the first draft found and skip revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A portfolio piece needs a reason and revision evidence.

answer.text: C. Choose a piece because it shows growth, strong craft, or clear publication potential.

feedback.text: Correct. Portfolio selection should be purposeful. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Choose no piece because portfolios cannot include creative work.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A portfolio is built from selected creative work.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q40

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U05_UA_Q40 A draft has a confusing ending and several spelling errors. What should the writer address first?\

answer.text: A. Correct spelling only and ignore the ending.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Polishing does not solve the larger meaning problem.

answer.text: B. Add random formatting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random formatting does not clarify the ending.

answer.text: C. Write the portfolio note before revising.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The note should reflect the final revised piece.

answer.text: D. Revise the ending so the reader understands the character's decision.

feedback.text: Correct. Meaning and purpose should be fixed before final polishing.
